# The front doors never spell out recursive self-improvement

## Context

Operator, 2026-09-23 ~01:15 CEST: after watching Fireship's *"Did Google just kickstart the intelligence explosion?"* (2026-09-17, 1.87M views; DeepMind's "Dream-RSI" turns an AI's discovery logs into a simulator), he asked whether `README.md` and `learn/benefits/Introduction.md` cover Neo's own loop enough. Measured tonight on `dev@e66b6f8142`: they cover the mechanism and never the words.

The post itself is #19058 (drafter @neo-fable-clio, under #13383; #19057 was its duplicate and is closed); its PR expands `gated-RSI` in `README.md` at first use. This ticket covers the Introduction side, which #19058 names as out of its scope.

## The Problem

- `README.md` uses "gated-RSI" five times and never expands it — handled by #19058's PR, not here.
- `learn/benefits/Introduction.md` §11 explains the loop in depth — typed gap signals, `RemDigestion`, `GoldenPathSynthesizer`, the "explain me" illustration — and uses "recursively improve" once, in its final sentence. §9 names two wrong shelves ("JavaScript framework", "single-assistant memory") and not the third the paper's readers bring: RSI as an exploration-policy optimizer.
- `.github/VISION.md`: no match for `recursive` or `self-improv`.

A reader who arrives from that video and searches the Introduction for "recursive self-improvement" finds one adverb. The vocabulary bridge from the world's term to Neo's term ("Dream Pipeline", "Golden Path") is missing, in both directions.

## The Architectural Reality

- The `neo-identity-update` skill governs framing changes across README, VISION, `learn/benefits` and the portal: facts single-source, framing audience-segmented against the canonical apex, never "framework".
- The mechanism's home is the Brain's [Dream Pipeline guide](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/dev/learn/agentos/DreamPipeline.md); the front doors point, they do not restate.
- The honest boundary must travel with the words: Neo's loop is institution-level (substrate improves under a human merge gate), not model-level; #19058's comparison section is the reference. Introduction §11 already carries that boundary; the new sentences must not widen it.

## The Fix

One documentation PR, after #19058's post has a URL to point at:

1. `learn/benefits/Introduction.md` §11: one sentence naming what the section describes in plain words — gated recursive self-improvement at the institution level — in the section's existing voice, linking the post.
2. `learn/benefits/Introduction.md` §9: the third wrong shelf, in one sentence: RSI as a replay-simulator policy optimizer is not the object here; the object is an institution's memory ranking its own next move.
3. `.github/VISION.md`: check whether the apex needs the same one line; add it only if the apex already claims the loop.
4. The lint-enforced integrity fingerprint in §10 is regenerated the way the guide prescribes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 Introduction §11 names recursive self-improvement in one sentence without adding a claim §11 does not already make, and links #19058's post.
- [ ] AC-2 Introduction §9 names the third wrong shelf in one sentence.
- [ ] AC-3 A search of the Introduction for "recursive self-improvement" hits; the "framework" count is unchanged.
- [ ] AC-4 The §10 integrity fingerprint matches the new byte count and line count.
- [ ] AC-5 VISION.md is either unchanged with the reason recorded in the PR, or carries the same one line.

## Out of Scope

- The blog post (#19058) and the README expansion (in #19058's PR).
- Any new capability claim; the loop's current degraded state is the post's chapter, not a front-door sentence.

## Related

#19058 (the post; README line lands there) · #13383 · `learn/benefits/Introduction.md` §9 / §11 · `.github/VISION.md` · Brain Dream Pipeline guide · #9738 · #9747
